name: Ranu Uniyal

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Ranu Uniyal writes poetry in English and Hindi. Her university biography records her work in English at the University of Lucknow and a doctorate from the University of Hull. Her academic interests include women’s writing, disability studies and poetry. Her collections include Across the Divide, December Poems, The Day We Went Strawberry Picking in Scarborough and Saeeda Ke Ghar.

The opening passage of “Plums versus Pullum” recalls fruit from Ranikhet, the streets of Almora and a mother’s kitchen. “At Kedarnath” turns to the force of a flood, using the imagery of Shiva and a river’s voice to question human disregard for the natural world.
